fields.pricingNote:
₹149 one time, per mock analysed. Not a subscription. A CAT aspirant takes somewhere between 15 and 40 mocks in a season and they do not want another ₹999 a month sitting on their card in December when they are writing the paper.

Why ₹149. The thing being bought is the two hours after the mock, not the mock. Everyone already has mocks — IMS, TIME, the free SIMCATs. What nobody does is sit down with the question-by-question timing log and work out that they lost 14 marks in DILR not because the sets were hard but because they spent 19 minutes on set 3 before abandoning it. A coaching class mentor charges ₹800 to ₹1,200 for one analysis session and you have to book it three days out; the aspirant is going to take the next mock on Sunday whether or not the mentor is free. ₹149 is roughly one-sixth of that and it is instant, which is the actual product. I also checked what they already spend without flinching: the ₹149 is the same as the Sunday Swiggy order they place after the mock.

What they give up by not paying: they take the next mock having learned nothing from this one. That is the real cost — not the report, the repeated mistake. Three of my first buyers described the same pattern of abandoning a DILR set too late in three consecutive mocks before they saw it written down.

notes: Number and unit are explicit (₹149, one time, per mock), the justification is buyer value against a named alternative's price, the cost of not buying is the repeated mistake rather than a feature list, and a one-time per-analysis price matches exactly what is shipped.
